title: Minecraft
blurb: The most played game ever made. Still the purest creative sandbox there is.

title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare III
blurb: Fast, twitchy military multiplayer with a yearly campaign and a huge seasonal grind.

title: Counter-Strike 2
blurb: The purest competitive shooter there is. Five rounds in you'll know if it's for you.

title: Call of Duty: Warzone
blurb: Free-to-play battle royale built on Call of Duty gunplay. Drop, loot, last squad standing.

title: Grand Theft Auto V
blurb: Three criminals, one city, and an online mode that refuses to die.

title: Call of Duty: Black Ops 6
blurb: Omnimovement shakes up the formula, plus the best Black Ops campaign in years and Zombies.

title: Valorant
blurb: Counter-Strike precision fused with hero abilities. Ruthlessly competitive, endlessly readable.

title: Fortnite
blurb: Build, edit, win. A constantly mutating cultural event that happens to be a great shooter.

title: Elden Ring
blurb: FromSoftware's world design at its peak. Punishing, mysterious, and impossible to put down.

title: The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim
blurb: Fifteen years on, still the definitive 'walk in any direction and find something' game.

title: Red Dead Redemption 2
blurb: Slow, deliberate, and unmatched as a world. Give it the first six hours.

title: The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt
blurb: The best side quests ever written. Every 'small' job turns into a short story.

title: Roblox
blurb: Millions of user-made games. A platform more than a game, and unavoidable.

title: Apex Legends
blurb: The most fluid movement in any battle royale, with squad pings that changed the genre.

title: Baldur's Gate 3
blurb: It says yes to everything you try. The high-water mark for player freedom.

title: Cyberpunk 2077
blurb: Night City is the most convincing city in games, and Phantom Liberty completes the redemption.

title: EA Sports FC 25
blurb: Football's annual ritual. Ultimate Team is the whole game and you know it.

title: Helldivers 2
blurb: Four players, one bug planet, endless friendly fire. Co-op comedy at its finest.

title: The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom
blurb: A physics sandbox with a Zelda skin. Whatever silly plan you have, it works.

title: Grand Theft Auto Online
blurb: Heists with friends, griefers in flying bikes. Still going after a decade.

title: Overwatch 2
blurb: Colourful 5v5 hero combat where team composition matters as much as your aim.

title: Genshin Impact
blurb: A genuinely gorgeous open world attached to a gacha. Free until it isn't.

title: God of War Ragnarök
blurb: Blockbuster spectacle with real emotional weight. The axe still feels perfect.

title: Stardew Valley
blurb: Quit your job, grow parsnips, romance a villager. Made by one person, and it shows.

title: Mario Kart 8 Deluxe
blurb: The best selling kart racer for a reason. Blue shells still ruin friendships.

title: Marvel Rivals
blurb: Overwatch with Marvel characters and destructible maps. Wildly popular for good reason.

title: Rainbow Six Siege
blurb: Breach a wall, hold an angle, win the round. Tense, slow, deeply tactical.

title: Rocket League
blurb: Car football. Easy to understand, impossible to master, perfect to watch.

title: Monster Hunter Wilds
blurb: Learn one monster for forty hours, then wear it as a hat. Deeply satisfying loop.

title: Destiny 2
blurb: Sci-fi gunfeel that has no equal, wrapped in a loot grind that will eat your year.

title: The Last of Us Part II
blurb: Uncomfortable on purpose. The most technically astonishing narrative game of its generation.

title: Terraria
blurb: Minecraft's 2D cousin with far better bosses and a real progression arc.

title: Super Smash Bros. Ultimate
blurb: Every character. Every stage. The definitive couch multiplayer game.

title: Pokémon Scarlet & Violet
blurb: Technically rough, genuinely fun. The open-world direction is the right one.

title: World of Warcraft
blurb: Twenty years of raid nights. Still the benchmark for endgame group content.

title: Resident Evil 4 Remake
blurb: The remake that improved on a classic. Tense, ridiculous and endlessly replayable.

title: DOOM Eternal
blurb: A violent rhythm game disguised as a shooter. Keep moving or die.

title: Diablo IV
blurb: Click demons, get shinier trousers, repeat. The seasonal treadmill done at AAA scale.

title: Marvel's Spider-Man 2
blurb: Web-swinging is still the best traversal in games. Pure joy to just move around.

title: Hollow Knight: Silksong
blurb: Faster, harder, and worth every year of the wait.

title: Balatro
blurb: Poker hands as a roguelike. You will lose entire evenings to this.

title: Final Fantasy XIV
blurb: The rare MMO with a story worth the subscription. The free trial is famously generous.

title: Hogwarts Legacy
blurb: The castle is the real star. Wandering the corridors is worth the price alone.

title: PUBG: Battlegrounds
blurb: The original battle royale. Slower, heavier and more nerve-shredding than its rivals.

title: Fallout 4
blurb: Weakest Fallout writing, strongest Fallout shooting, and settlement building is a trap.

title: Ghost of Tsushima
blurb: The most beautiful open world Sony has made, and duels that feel like cinema.

title: Palworld
blurb: Creature collecting meets factory automation meets guns. Somehow it works.

title: Hollow Knight
blurb: Melancholy bug kingdom, brutal bosses, and a map you slowly learn to love.

title: Animal Crossing: New Horizons
blurb: A gentle island routine. No fail state, no pressure, just debt to a raccoon.

title: Forza Horizon 5
blurb: The most relaxing racing game there is. Just drive around Mexico with music on.

title: Dark Souls III
blurb: The most refined Dark Souls combat, and a farewell tour of the whole series.

title: Dead by Daylight
blurb: Four survivors versus one killer. A whole hobby's worth of licensed horror crossovers.

title: Battlefield 1
blurb: World War I as a muddy, thunderous spectacle. Still the series' most atmospheric entry.

title: Halo Infinite
blurb: The gunplay finally sings again, and the grappling hook makes the sandbox playful.

title: Persona 5 Royal
blurb: A hundred hours of high-school life and stylish heists. Absurdly confident presentation.

title: Assassin's Creed Shadows
blurb: Feudal Japan at last, with a shinobi and a samurai who play completely differently.

title: Rust
blurb: Wake up naked, get killed by a stranger with a rock. Peak online cruelty.

title: Portal 2
blurb: Perfect puzzle pacing and perfect jokes. The co-op campaign is a separate treasure.

title: NBA 2K25
blurb: Superb on-court simulation attached to an aggressive currency store.

title: Super Mario Odyssey
blurb: Movement so good you'll jump around for fun. Pure, uncynical delight.

title: Black Myth: Wukong
blurb: Spectacular boss fights rooted in Chinese mythology. A genuine technical showcase.

title: Final Fantasy VII Rebirth
blurb: Enormous, messy, sincere. The combat system is the best in the series.

title: Battlefield 2042
blurb: 128-player warfare with vehicles, collapsing skyscrapers and squad play at enormous scale.

title: Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice
blurb: Deflect, don't dodge. A rhythm of steel that clicks and then never lets go.

title: Horizon Forbidden West
blurb: Fighting robot dinosaurs with a bow remains an inspired idea, executed beautifully.

title: Vampire Survivors
blurb: Barely a game and completely irresistible. Screen full of numbers, brain full of dopamine.

title: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33
blurb: Turn-based combat with real-time dodges, and art direction that stops you dead.

title: Escape from Tarkov
blurb: Brutally realistic extraction shooter where losing a raid costs you everything you carried.

title: Lethal Company
blurb: Collect scrap for the Company, lose your friends to a monster, laugh anyway.

title: Titanfall 2
blurb: Wall-run into a mech. The campaign is a six-hour masterclass in level design.

title: Fallout: New Vegas
blurb: The gold standard for reactive RPG writing. Your choices genuinely rearrange the world.

title: Path of Exile 2
blurb: A skill tree the size of a country. For people who read spreadsheets for fun.

title: Resident Evil Village
blurb: Four wildly different horror styles in one game. Yes, that lady.

title: Valheim
blurb: Viking survival with genuinely beautiful lighting and satisfying building physics.

title: Hades II
blurb: Dying is progress. The writing and art are absurdly good for a roguelike.

title: Among Us
blurb: Lie to your friends in space. Better with voice chat and a shaky moral compass.

title: Mass Effect Legendary Edition
blurb: Three games, one save file, and a crew you'll still think about years later.

title: The Finals
blurb: Every wall, floor and ceiling can come down. Chaos as a core mechanic.

title: Bloodborne
blurb: Victorian cosmic horror with the most aggressive combat FromSoft ever built.

title: Uncharted 4: A Thief's End
blurb: A summer blockbuster you hold the controller for. The jeep chase alone justifies it.

title: Phasmophobia
blurb: Ghost hunting with friends. Half detective work, half everyone screaming at once.

title: Subnautica
blurb: Ocean exploration that turns genuine fear of the deep into wonder. Play it blind.

title: Split Fiction
blurb: Hazelight again: two players, sci-fi and fantasy worlds, endless mechanical invention.

title: Street Fighter 6
blurb: The most welcoming fighting game ever made, with genuine depth underneath.

title: Borderlands 3
blurb: A billion guns and a co-op loop that turns numbers going up into a lifestyle.

title: NieR: Automata
blurb: Play it to the real ending. It uses the medium in ways nothing else does.

title: Deep Rock Galactic
blurb: Space dwarves mine procedural caves. Rock and stone, genuinely one of the best co-op games.

title: Divinity: Original Sin 2
blurb: Elemental chaos and systemic sandbox combat. Best played with a scheming friend.

title: Silent Hill 2
blurb: Psychological horror about grief, remade with care. Heavy in the best way.

title: Sid Meier's Civilization VII
blurb: One more turn. It's 4am. You know exactly what this game is.

title: Celeste
blurb: A hard platformer about anxiety, with the kindest assist options in the business.

title: It Takes Two
blurb: Mandatory two-player. Every level introduces a brand new mechanic and then drops it.

title: Undertale
blurb: You don't have to kill anything. It remembers what you do.

title: Fall Guys
blurb: Sixty beans, one crown, endless indignity. Wonderfully silly.

title: Warframe
blurb: Space ninja power fantasy. Free, enormous, and impossible to explain to newcomers.

title: Factorio
blurb: The factory must grow. Genuinely one of the most addictive games ever built.

title: Football Manager 2024
blurb: A spreadsheet that will make you feel real emotions about a Norwegian left-back.

title: Dead Cells
blurb: Buttery combat and short runs. The perfect 'one more go' game.

title: Slay the Spire
blurb: The deckbuilder that spawned a genre. Every run is a puzzle you build yourself.

title: Tekken 8
blurb: Aggression is rewarded. Also there is a bear and a man who is also a dinosaur.

title: The Elder Scrolls Online
blurb: Skyrim-shaped MMO you can genuinely play solo. Zone stories are the highlight.

title: Left 4 Dead 2
blurb: Four survivors, a horde, and the most quietly brilliant AI director in games.

title: Death Stranding 2: On the Beach
blurb: A delivery sim about connection. Either the most boring or most moving thing you'll play.

title: Dead Space
blurb: Sound design that will make you check behind you. Still the best sci-fi horror.

title: Sons of the Forest
blurb: Build a fortress before the cannibals find it. Kelvin is doing his best.

title: Total War: Warhammer III
blurb: Turn-based empire building plus thousands of models colliding in real time.

title: RimWorld
blurb: A story generator disguised as a colony sim. Everything that goes wrong is a story.

title: Disco Elysium
blurb: The best writing in any video game. You investigate a murder and also yourself.

title: Mortal Kombat 1
blurb: Absurd gore, a surprisingly good story mode, and tag-team assists.

title: Gran Turismo 7
blurb: A love letter to car culture. The physics reward patience over aggression.

title: Dave the Diver
blurb: Dive by day, run a sushi restaurant by night. Should not work, absolutely does.

title: Astro Bot
blurb: Pure joy, start to finish. The most purely delightful platformer since Odyssey.

title: Control
blurb: Telekinesis in a shifting brutalist office building. Throw everything at everything.

title: DayZ
blurb: Long stretches of nothing punctuated by the most tense encounters in gaming.

title: XCOM 2
blurb: 95% hit chance means nothing. You will name your soldiers and you will mourn them.

title: Hunt: Showdown 1896
blurb: Bayou monster hunting where every distant gunshot means another team heard you too.

title: Dragon Age: The Veilguard
blurb: Slick action combat and a companion cast that carries the whole thing.

title: Alan Wake 2
blurb: A survival horror art film. Genuinely unlike anything else, and the musical level is unforgettable.

title: Grounded
blurb: Honey I Shrunk the Kids as survival. Arachnophobia slider is a genuinely kind touch.

title: ARK: Survival Ascended
blurb: Tame a dinosaur, build a base, lose it all to a raid. Enormous time sink.

title: StarCraft II
blurb: The most demanding competitive game ever made. The campaigns are great too.

title: Risk of Rain 2
blurb: Stack items until you break physics. Best played with three friends.

title: Outer Wilds
blurb: A 22-minute time loop and a solar system of secrets. Do not read anything about it.

title: Splatoon 3
blurb: Ink the floor, not the enemy. The most original shooter concept in years.

title: LEGO Fortnite
blurb: A surprisingly full survival crafting game bolted onto Fortnite.

title: Age of Empires IV
blurb: Classic RTS done right, with documentary campaigns that are actually worth watching.

title: Cities: Skylines II
blurb: Traffic management as a lifestyle. Deeply calming until the sewage backs up.

title: Crusader Kings III
blurb: Medieval dynasty roleplay where your heir is an idiot and it's your fault.

title: Cult of the Lamb
blurb: Adorable animals, sinister cult management. The tonal clash is the whole joke.

title: Metroid Dread
blurb: Tight, tense and fast. The best 2D Metroid since Super.

title: Lies of P
blurb: Pinocchio as a soulslike, and a shockingly confident one.

title: Stellaris
blurb: Build a galactic empire, then discover something worse lives on the rim.

title: Blue Prince
blurb: Draft rooms to build a mansion and uncover its secret. You'll need a notebook.

title: The Outlast Trials
blurb: Cold War human experiments as co-op horror. Relentlessly unpleasant, on purpose.

title: Papers, Please
blurb: Glory to Arstotzka. Stamping passports has never been this morally exhausting.

title: PowerWash Simulator
blurb: Clean dirty things. Astonishingly effective as stress relief.

title: Frostpunk 2
blurb: City building where every law you pass costs someone something. Bleak and brilliant.

title: Tunic
blurb: A cute fox adventure hiding one of the cleverest puzzle games ever made.

title: Return of the Obra Dinn
blurb: Deduce how sixty sailors died. The most satisfying detective work in games.

title: Assetto Corsa Competizione
blurb: The sim racer's sim racer. Bring a wheel or don't bother.

title: A Short Hike
blurb: Climb a mountain, chat to some animals, be done in ninety minutes. Perfect.

title: Spiritfarer
blurb: A cozy game about dying. You'll cry, and the boat is lovely.

title: Unpacking
blurb: Unpack boxes, learn a whole life story from the objects. Quietly devastating.

title: Baba Is You
blurb: You rewrite the rules of each level. Will make you feel stupid then brilliant.

title: Slime Rancher 2
blurb: Vacuum up adorable slimes on a pastel alien world. Genuinely calming.

title: Coral Island
blurb: Stardew with better graphics and a coral reef to restore. Very comfortable.

title: Dorfromantik
blurb: Place tiles, build a peaceful landscape. A puzzle game that never rushes you.

title: Chants of Sennaar
blurb: Decipher invented languages by context alone. Makes you feel like a genius.
